sections.title: P2.7 — self-check against actual migrations
sections.text:
The frozen item and OPUS are interpreted with accepted D18. PostgreSQL 0.2 upgrade is
the historical-data lane; SQLite/PostgreSQL are verified fresh-install lanes. MySQL
fresh installation retains the specifically permitted P2.1 defect, owned by P8.1.
MySQL 0.2 upgrade is excluded by D09 and is not claimed supported.

sections.title: Invariants and evidence
sections.text:
- Preserve historical identifiers, values and row ownership through table/column
  renames. Both committed bigint/ULID dumps exercise migrate, no-op migrate,
  replay of every new up, full upgrade-batch rollback and re-upgrade.
  Canon03UpgradeTest checks counts and each historical activity event mapping.
- Schema after either upgrade equals fresh schema for the same strategy: all
  column types/null/default/collation/generation metadata, indexes, named FKs,
  and PostgreSQL expression/predicate SQL. SchemaParityTest passes exactly;
  the measured P2.1 baseline contains zero differences for both fixtures.
- Fail before rename on unsafe legacy nodes/drives/files or revisionless documents.
  UpgradePreflightTest checks direct exception details and full artisan migration
  refusal. FixtureTestCase deliberately disables automatic setup migration, so
  unsafe historical fixtures actually reach the intended preflight test.
- Preserve all endpoint subscription elements, ordering, duplicates, wildcard and
  custom names. Only the exact event map changes. Batch size is 500. Historical
  scalar event columns convert in the same migration. Canon03UpgradeTest covers
  the fixture and a deliberately mixed list; the negative control disables only
  the endpoint UPDATE and must fail.
- No feature flag removes a canonical table. Node extra_data remains its actual
  existing flagged column until P4.1. CanonicalSchemaTest covers disabled flags.
- Keep REST storage_id, node_id, panel, version_no and content_sha256 names while
  reading canonical attributes. UploadSessionResource maps node_id to
  target_node_id; storage slug/storage_type return null after those columns are
  removed. Drive HTTP tests and MutationContractsTest exercise these shapes.
- A fresh install's rollback must drop the canonical base tables. New migration
  down methods distinguish a fresh batch from a historical upgrade batch using
  migration repository rows on the selected connection. Fresh down does not
  rename tables away from the base migration's dropTable targets.
- №3 runs before №4: historical revisions remain available for host-key conversion,
  including customized names. №2/№4 normalize physical constraints/index names
  and PostgreSQL serial sequence names. LegacyTableNamesUpgradeTest includes
  customized nodes and revisions, rollback, and a repeated upgrade.
- IDs.host_keys and P1 root/blob-scope behavior remain effective: declared
  PostgreSQL Upgrade+Schema lane passes without skips; the P1 regression grid
  supplements this with typed host keys, listing, races and CAS checks.

sections.title: Known risks
sections.text:
- Fixed: SQLite change() can rebuild partial uniqueness incorrectly. Canonical
  fresh migration №2 is a no-op; a renamed historical profile is changed only
  during the supported PostgreSQL upgrade. Exact parity includes predicates.
- Fixed: repeated upload-session index rename could produce target_target_node_id.
  The migration uses complete index names and direct up replay is checked.
- Fixed: Testbench's auto-migration rollback interfered with fixture-owned schemas.
  A dedicated FixtureTestCase only registers paths; each upgrade test owns cleanup.
- Deferred to P8.1: real MySQL fresh install fails with error 1215 while adding
  sibling_active STORED over a cascading parent_id FK. mysql-baseline-classification.json
  reproduces the same SQL on archived P2.1 product bytes and on this candidate.
  No successful full MySQL installation is claimed.
- Deferred to P4.1/P4.7: node current_version_id/file_id/deleted_at and document
  version storage remain historical by explicit scope exclusion.
- Deferred to P6.1: REST naming migration. The current JSON keys stay compatible.
- Explicitly irreversible: soft-deleted grants are deleted; dropped metadata and
  inheritance flags cannot be recovered by structural rollback. UPGRADE.md requires
  backup and explains this. Share revocation timestamps are preserved.
